sourceImagery: Uppsala kommun Ortofoto_2024 / Swescan; 0.25 m server export of 0.08 m native source
frame: EPSG:3006 using terrain reader exact legacy-grid bridge; no image fitting
sourceDates: DTM 2023-04-26/27; orthophoto product 2024 (exact flight date not exposed)
accuracy: Visual corroboration, not an independent surveyed accuracy assessment. Pixel spacing is not horizontal RMSE; accepted boundaries remain dated source derivatives.

decisions.reason: The laser candidate follows the visible basin; corrects coarse west and south polygon corners. Reed/water transition on east bank remains 1-3 m uncertain.
Candidate follows visible open-water edge more closely, especially tree-lined east bank. Some shore lies under canopy; retain 2-4 m uncertainty there.
Candidate improves south/west angular overshoot and retains the complete visible pond; water/reed transition remains approximate.
Candidate follows the complete visible pond and corrects coarse corners; small inward notch on NW bank remains below a few metres, not surveyed.
Candidate improves angular OSM overshoot and follows the visible basin. Broad extent consistent between 2023 laser and 2024 photograph.
Candidate removes obvious west and south OSM overshoot onto grass while preserving complete basin; vegetated northern head remains approximate.

Reject entire DTM replacement as generated: the morphology removes a real narrow NW inlet/secondary lobe visible behind a bridge in 2024 imagery. Main basin boundary is useful, but retain water connectivity and inlet geometry separately before adopting.
Reject: DTM threshold deletes NE pond lobe which visibly remains dark/vegetated water in 2024 photograph. A single strict height band is inadequate for this body.
Reject: DTM morphology truncates a real narrow SW inlet/channel visible in imagery. Basin-only tracing is not a complete water boundary.
Reject automatic replacement: surface is strongly vegetated and basin margin is not sufficiently separable from reeds; DTM plate alone cannot establish the current visible water/vegetation boundary.
Retain measured rough-ground swale as terrain evidence only. Imagery does not establish a continuous channel or watercourse; do not add stream water or hazard marking.
Reject watercourse identity: candidate follows cart road cutting and road edge through rocky woodland. Possible local roadside drainage cannot justify the full derived polyline.

Reject: candidate crosses a clearly visible greenside bunker and then connects it to the existing mapped ditch. This is a least-cost path false connection; bunker depressions must be excluded before ditch tracing.

OSM ring overlays a pale, irregular rough/bare patch without clear manicured sand surface. Laser is convex relative to rim (-0.373 m), unlike an ordinary bunker. Could be rocky ground or a disused bunker; requires club or stronger material evidence before removing or relabelling.

OSM ring contains a conspicuous southwest lobe of green grass beyond the visible sand. Removing that grassy lobe and tracing the visible sand edge is a supported correction. Tree shadow makes the north/east edge partly uncertain.
